issues.description: Repeated nil-guard boilerplate across ~20 accessors instead of one shared helper
issues.detail: Both reviewers flag the same copy-pasted pattern (`var s []X; if x != nil { s = ... }; return seq.NewFixedSlice(s, ...)`) in every getter. The fix is one helper — make seq.NewFixedSlice tolerate nil, or add a nilSafeSlice wrapper — so the contract is enforced once instead of relying on every future getter author to remember.

issues.description: Two parallel zero-checks (f == nil vs t.IsZero()) instead of one canonical guard
issues.detail: File uses `if f != nil`; Type/Member/Oneof/ReservedName/Element use `if !x.IsZero()`. These are two different predicates for the same abstract notion of an absent value. A single canonical predicate across IR node types would prevent drift as new accessors are added.

issues.description: Zero-value contract is implicit and only enforced by reflection; should be specified in package docs
issues.detail: The PR establishes a real ADT contract — accessors on a zero/nil receiver return the zero value of the result type — but that contract lives only in a reflective test. State it at the package or IsZero level (a doc.go) so future methods know the precondition, rather than discovering violations after the fact.

issues.description: Test addition and ~20 behavioral nil-guard fixes should be separate commits
issues.detail: The commit mixes "add zero test" with a wide spray of panic fixes. Land the test first, then each panic fix as its own diff with a one-line justification. As submitted, a future bisect on any regression points uselessly at the test commit.

issues.description: ValueNodeIndex returns -1 sentinel, inconsistent with other zero accessors
issues.detail: Every other zero accessor returns the type's zero value, but ValueNodeIndex returns -1. Callers now must know two sentinels (0 valid, -1 zero). Either return (int, bool), add a HasValueNode predicate, or pick one convention and document it on the type itself rather than just a comment.

issues.description: Reflection-driven zero test silently skips methods with parameters and under-specifies multi-return contracts
issues.detail: testZeroAny filters to NumIn()==1, so accessors taking arguments (e.g. ImportFor) are never exercised. It also treats any Len()==0 as success and may pass on multi-return or interface-returning methods that still violate intent. Add an explicit allowlist of skipped methods and audit list per type.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this PR is doing the right kind of work — establishing a zero-value contract across IR accessors and adding a reflective test to enforce it. The execution has consistent weaknesses: the same nil-guard boilerplate is copy-pasted across twenty methods instead of captured in one helper, the guard idiom is non-uniform (`f == nil` vs `IsZero()`), and the contract is implicit (only the test states it). The ValueNodeIndex -1 sentinel breaks the otherwise uniform convention. Verdict: sound in intent, needs refactor and documentation before landing; consider splitting the test from the fixes.
